detail: (prop type - prop value)
notes: Properties have become a special (reserved) data object, and thus its further use as a normal action (which can be renamed, removed...) is discouraged. It would seem needed in some cases, e.g. when attaching a prop to a related (same content) statement, where the same content is used in the answer (quod sic) but then is extended with some detail not contained in the question ("et possunt esse anni .X. vel circa"), but there again, "has" construction is not built for second-level properties (where to attach it, to a1 or a2 - neither is correct?), so has is discouraged even in those cases, and instead, use a dummy statement without verb, which attaches the prop to the source in the role of pseudo-actant.

Property type = actant1, property value = actant2. Some attributes can have time, e.g. someone can be a resident of Milan (or be unmarried and then married) at some time. Location, by contrast, is not allowed: for office of "inquisitor heretice pravitatis" in Lombardy and March of Genoa, a C should be used which already holds this "in Lombardy and March of Genoa", which is a subset of "inquisitor heretice pravitatis" more generally.
History: The label of this A (legacy ID A0093) was "has attribute", then "has property", then "has" only (see https://docs.google.com/document/d/1GMAsDJJIa4YuOKwiDLQKt6pSPud71lhUNf3sb6XkGyU/edit).

notes: The precision is relative to the class of the Location. E.g., it is expected that if the coordinates have localisation precision "precise" and the class is “settlement”, the coordinates will fall within the area of the (medieval) settlement. But for a Location with class “house”, “precise” would mean that it is precisely localized at the granularity of houses! This means that a medieval house will rarely have localisation precision precise; rather, it will either be localized to the settlement, one of its gates or one of its parishes, and the localisation precision will be “approximate”, or there will be no coordinates but a location relation stating that the gate is “SRP next to” it or that the house has as its “superordinate location” the settlement. A church will often have localisation precision "precise", since its location is often known or it is still standing.
